answer: An AI‑agent’s reputation token is minted on a karst‑like ledger that only issues one token per unique cryptographic proof of hardware attestation; each token is staked on a jetty contract that automatically ages it, granting incremental voting weight while a decay function withdraws weight after 30 days of inactivity, leaving the token in a hollow state that cannot be reused. To launch a Sybil attack, an adversary must purchase, certify, and lock up a distinct hardware root of trust for every fake identity, incurring a minimum cost of $1,200 USD plus a 30‑day bonding period per node.
